text:
Rubén Darío has died,

the one of precious stones!


Brother, how many nights your spirit and mine,

joined for flight like two eager wings,

wanted to sound the dark Enigma hungrily,

beyond the stars and the nebulae!


Rubén Darío has died,

the one of precious stones!


How many intense years we lived beside the Seine,

setting our youthful verses

in the gold of a common ideal,

which sometimes we saw spring

like two roses blooming at once from a rosebush!


Today your restless life, like a wild torrent,

has emptied into the Sea of Causes; now you rest

your wandering feet on the cold islet

painted by Böcklin... now you know all things!


Rubén Darío has died,

the one of precious stones!


My belated waves follow yours; but soon,

in the unfathomable and eternal sea of everything,

my spirit will be sated with what I wish to know:

the How and the Why, Essence and Mode.


And you, as in Lutetia on those mysterious afternoons

when we thought together beside the lyrical River,

will have to guide me... I will go where you dare,

to steal together from the musical void

and from the choir of the orbs their portentous keys...


Rubén Darío has died,

the one of precious stones!

translation.title: Rubén Darío Has Died...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Nervo’s repeated elegy refrain and the shared astronomical and musical metaphors for Darío’s death.
